To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the best dataset for benchmarking localization at intersections is the KITTI odometry dataset, and 2) the best dataset that is not yet available is a dataset from a vehicle with a stereo camera that is approaching an unstructured intersection.

(i) the KITTI stereo dataset has the most complete and reliable information on ground-truth position, (ii) the ground-truth information is available only for a few sequences and for the first few meters of each of them, (iii) the KITTTI stereo sequences are of very low resolution and the ground-truth is available only for the first few seconds of each of them.

the dataset we propose is the only one that contains sequences of a moving road vehicle approaching an intersection, and that the KITTI sequences are the only ones that are suitable for the task of online vehicle localization.
